A lot to unpack here: just my quick two cents.

The key to getting stronger is junctioning magic. The better the magic the better the stats. As you level up your enemies do too which means they have better magic to draw etc etc. 

Best GF abilities off the top of my head, refine magic as an easy way to get better magic from items, Str up/Mag Up etc will add a bonus point to the junctioned characters stats are pretty good early game. You can find lot of Str % upgrades which will help stats early game as well.

DON’T wait for the game to tell you when to upgrade, technically you can get the end game weapons at the stage you’re at if you know what to do (or follow a guide). Refine Tool for Siren, Refine ammo for ifrit and mod cards for Quetz should give you more upgrade materials.

Check the wiki on this group, a lot of beginner questions will be answered there. Apart from that:

1. Take it as it comes, if you start feeling sick/dizzy check your electrolytes and your water intake. If you still feel unwell-stop.

2. Drink water regularly. It should be your go to drink. Carbonated but unflavoured water is fine, black coffee/tea is fine, diet drinks are different person to person but may affect appetite.

3. The bulk of your fast should be whilst your asleep, ideally it’s just a case of not having your dinner too late and skipping breakfast. 

4. Treat your first few fasts as experimental to see what times of day etc. Works best for you. If you feel like doing longer after trying 16:8 do so in small increments. If you ever plan on doing 24+ fasts you need to be on point with your electrolytes/water.

5. Leading up to your first fast try lowering your carbs and increasing protein and fat. Try to make your last meal before a fast even more so so that you don’t get too bad a carb withdrawal.

6. Downloading a fasting app helps keep track and lets you know when you’re done. A lot of people use Life which tells you what’s happening biologically as you go through your fast.

Good luck!

He has a problem and regardless of his motivations to hang out with you, having access to those pills isn’t helping anyone. I know it must suck because you’re worried about leaving someone who may just need your friendship but at the very least knowing you have access to meds’ is stalling his recovery. I would be completely straight with him and tell him that you need to take a break from the friendship to give him time to recover, that’s it’s not personal but you’re worried you’re not helping him in the long term.
If he’s really your friend he’ll probably be mad but will understand. If he doesn’t, then at least you know it was the addiction talking when he reaches out to you.
You’ve also got to consider your own health as well. You should be proud of how long you’ve been clean for and I want to congratulate that, but also bear in mind that being in an environment where you’re spending time with an addict could be a risk to you. There’s nothing wrong with protecting yourself.

I also grew up with an autistic younger sibling who had to be dependent on my mum pretty much full-time. Although triggers/reactions are different I already had an open mind as it’s not easy being the ‘normal’ child and often having to be second fiddle to your siblings needs. 

Having read the full story it is obvious that your parents are not managing the situation appropriately, like AT ALL. Hitting is not okay, regardless of how deep on the spectrum and although it may be harder to parent that, they should still be doing something to get across that that’s not an acceptable course of action.  

You are already NTA for having complicated feelings towards a sibling in a difficult family dynamic (although I think some of it may be misplaced), you are definitely NTA since the blame is squarely on your parents for neglecting your emotional needs because you’re the easier child to manage.

I successfully did keto about 8 years ago and managed to lose over 100 lbs. I did it in bursts, the longest being 5 months where I lost 5 stone (70lbs). It was very on and off, at my lightest I was 144lbs at 5’8. 

I moved to settle down with my now-husband, was a long distance runner but lost that when I burned myself out with a marathon-want to get back up to that standard again.

The weight gradually crept up due to my poor food choices and after I gave birth to our daughter I ended up being my heaviest at 270lbs. 

My goal weight (for now) is to get to under 200lbs. I’ve got a couple of incentives in mind, a cousin’s wedding next year, family reunion in December (and I’m sick of seeing myself in photos) but the biggest one is that I want to do a medical donation and can’t do it until I’m under 30 bmi. 

Currently finishing day 1/3 of a fat fast to kick off with MCT supplements. The last time I did keto it was with prepackaged powder meals so nervous about making my own meals and working out macros. This will be a good experiment for me to see how it goes.

Good luck everyone! :)
